article_title: GitHub Actions Xcode 27 Runner Image Reaches General Availability on Apple Silicon Only, With an OpenSSL 4 Default Change Due November 2

content_preview.title: GitHub Actions Xcode 27 Runner Image Reaches General Availability on Apple Silicon Only, With an OpenSSL 4 Default Change Due November 2
content_preview.summary: GitHub's Xcode 27 runner image for Actions is now generally available on arm64 runners only; a separate runner-images notice plans to make OpenSSL 4 the default from November 2.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

GitHub announced on October 15, 2026 that the Xcode 27 runner image for GitHub Actions is generally available. In its [changelog entry](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-15-xcode-27-runner-image-generally-available), GitHub says users can now use the image "to build and test your Apple applications in GitHub Actions," and that the image was previously in public preview. The image is limited to Apple Silicon runners, and a separate runner-images notice flags a default-tool change...

editor_notes.source_verification: All five sources are GitHub first-party (github.blog and github.com, both on the allowlist). Manifest: all five status 200, no archive fallback, suspicious_patterns null for all. Snapshots read (gunzip + text extraction) and then live-checked via GitHub API. source-0 (Oct 15 changelog, dated 'October 15, 2026'): confirms GA, 'You can now use the generally available Xcode 27 runner image to build and test your Apple applications in GitHub Actions' (quote 1 verbatim), 'Previously in public preview', macOS 27 + Xcode 27 toolchain and Apple SDKs, labels xcode-27 / xcode-27-xlarge, 'If you already use these labels, you don't need to change your workflows', 'one major Xcode version rather than targeting a specific operating system version', and 'The image is available on Apple Silicon (arm64) runners only, not Intel runners' - Intel is explicitly excluded in the source. source-1 (Sep 10 changelog): 'The image previously ran on macOS 26' (quote 3 verbatim, article quotes the fragment 'previously ran on macOS 26'); also states arm64-only. source-2 (issue #14404): opened Jul 16, 2026, Target date 'Thursday, July 16, 2026', 'The purpose of a Preview is to collect feedback on an image before it is released to GA', 'Edit 2026.09.16 xcode-27 image now uses MacOS 27 OS as its base OS' - all match. Live API: issue still open, last updated Oct 6 (a comment); body still carries stale 'macOS 26 with Xcode 27' text, which the article does not repeat. source-3 (issue #14856, opened Oct 6, 2026): default openssl changes from 3.x to 4.x on macOS 26 Intel/Arm64 and Xcode 27 Arm64; OpenSSL 4 already installed; OpenSSL 3 remains via versioned Homebrew prefix; no change on macOS 14/15, Ubuntu, Windows; 'rollout is planned to begin on November 2, 2026 and complete by November 8, 2026, subject to compatibility validation' (quote 2 'subject to compatibility validation' verbatim); possible-impact and mitigation text match the article's paraphrase. State at writing time vs now (live GitHub API at review, 2026-10-19): created_at = updated_at = 2026-10-06T11:40:38Z, zero comments, no label changes beyond OS: macOS / Announcement; the plan (Nov 2-8) is unchanged and the issue has not been edited since opening. source-4 (xcode-27-arm64-Readme.md): image version 20261012.0260.1, macOS 27.0.1, Xcode table: 27.2 (beta) 27B5028f, 27.1 27A9275 at Xcode_27.1_Release_Candidate.app, 27.0 (default) 27A266a. Article states 27.0 default, 27.1 with Release Candidate app path, 27.2 listed as beta - correct, and appropriately hedges that versions change with image updates (readme last updated Oct 16 per git history). Readme also lists OpenSSL 3.6.5 and openssl@4 4.0.3, consistent with the 'already installed' claim.
